coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app's riskiest logic — the whole data-transformation layer, URL state, and the sorting comparator — has zero test coverage; the only guard is the external acceptance suite.

behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests at all, so there is nothing to assess as behavioural; scored 1 per the rubric for no tests.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:70-77 — cache-eviction-on-error is load-bearing and two deletable lines from a permanent poison

regression_power.rationale: No test would fail if any covered-behaviour bug was introduced, because none exist; several subtle invariants (null-sort direction, cache eviction, dedupe levels) look like cleanup targets and would regress silently.

evidence: app/ — zero test files, no low-value padding either
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise; scored the rubric's neutral 3 for the no-tests case.

findings.issue: The entire data layer (470 lines of fetching, mapping, deduping, sorting) has no tests, despite being almost entirely unit-testable pure transformation over fixture JSON.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest with fixture snapshots of PokeAPI responses (already available under tests/fixtures/ and data/) covering idFromUrl, latestFlavor, loadHomeIndex, cardsFromPokemonRefs, and getPokemonPage's move-table assembly.

findings.issue: URL filter state is managed with raw window.history.pushState/replaceState plus a hand-rolled popstate listener instead of Qwik City's navigate API, and none of it (back/forward restoration, param omission, page reset) is tested.
findings.suggestion: Prefer useNavigate()/location.url for URL mutations, and add Playwright tests for back/forward restoring filter state and for buildHomeUrl omitting default params.

findings.issue: The 'missing values sort last in both directions' invariant is implemented by returning 1 for nulls while ignoring the direction factor; this looks like a bug and will be 'fixed' in a refactor with no test failing.
findings.suggestion: Extract compareRows into lib and unit-test it explicitly: nulls last for both ascending and descending on numeric and string keys.

findings.issue: Move dedupe keeps the minimum level via a compound condition (existing.level === null || level < existing.level); a refactor could keep the first, last, or wrong entry and show duplicate rows or wrong levels.
findings.suggestion: Unit test getPokemonPage against a fixture where the same move appears multiple times in one version group/method.

findings.issue: Cache eviction on fetch failure is what keeps a transient API 500 from being cached forever; deleting the catch block would silently poison the in-memory cache for the server's lifetime.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that a failed fetch is not cached and succeeds on retry (mock fetch with a then-successful response).

findings.issue: Type-page moves are sorted by humanized label via localeCompare while the spec says sorted alphabetically by name; hyphen/space handling can produce a different order, and no test pins the ordering.
findings.suggestion: Sort by API name (or assert both orderings agree on real data) and unit-test with names containing hyphens and apostrophes.

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000) is duplicated in three places (generation loop, typesByPokemon, cardsFromPokemonRefs); a partial refactor would let Megas leak into one list but not others, unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single isAlternateForm/idFromUrl guard helper and test that a fixture with id 10033 is excluded from every list.

findings.issue: Invalid ?game= values silently fall back to the latest version group; a refactor could 404 or throw instead, and no test covers the fallback.
findings.suggestion: Unit test getPokemonPage with gameQuery='nonexistent' asserting the default is selected.

findings.issue: humanize/dexNumber/displayNumber are pure spec-critical formatters (em dash, #0025 padding, whitespace collapse upstream) with zero tests despite being the cheapest coverage in the codebase.
findings.suggestion: Add a trivial Vitest file covering mr-mime, thunder-punch, dex 25, and null values.

findings.issue: No test script, runner, or harness is configured, so even adding tests later requires bootstrapping from zero.
findings.suggestion: Install Vitest (and Playwright for the sort/URL interactions) and wire npm test scripts in app/package.json.

summary: The app ships with zero tests of its own: no runner, no script, no test files. Since the acceptance suite is external and non-owned, every subtle invariant in the codebase — direction-ignoring null sorts, cache eviction on error, move dedupe levels, raw-history URL state coupled to Qwik City internals — is one innocent refactor away from a silent regression. The data layer in app/src/lib/api.ts is almost entirely pure transformation over fixture data and would be cheap to cover with Vitest; nothing was done.
